title: Jobs & CronJobs
intro: Not everything runs forever. Jobs run a task to completion once; CronJobs run one on a schedule.

steps.prompt: Run a one-off Job named 'db-migrate' using the migrate-tool image.
steps.explanation: A Job creates a pod, waits for it to exit successfully, and is done — no restarting on success like a Deployment would.
steps.why: This is different from 'kubectl run' — run makes a bare pod that's expected to keep running; a Job is specifically for something meant to finish.

steps.explanation: COMPLETIONS 1/1 means the task ran and exited 0 — done.
steps.why: 'kubectl get pods' would also show the underlying pod, but 'get jobs' gives you the completion status directly instead of having to interpret pod phase yourself.

steps.prompt: Create a CronJob named 'nightly-backup' using the backup-tool image, running at 2am every day.
steps.explanation: The schedule is standard cron syntax — this one means minute 0, hour 2, every day.
steps.why: A CronJob is really just a template that stamps out a new Job on schedule — everything you just learned about Jobs applies to each run it creates.

steps.prompt: You don't want to wait until 2am to test it — trigger a manual run of the CronJob right now.
steps.explanation: This creates a Job using the CronJob's pod template, immediately, without touching the schedule.
steps.why: This is the standard way to test a CronJob's behavior without waiting for its actual schedule or temporarily editing the cron expression.
